plain: The claim is that Francis Crick, the scientist who co-discovered the double helix structure of DNA, wrote a paper in 1973 proposing directed panspermia, the idea that life on Earth was seeded here on purpose from elsewhere. Michels brings it up himself in several episodes. In one he says Crick "decided to write a paper on directed panspermia." In another, talking with the biologist Rupert Sheldrake, he calls Crick a former associate of Sheldrake's and mentions a second date, 1981. In a third he gives no date or paper and says only that Crick proposed the idea. The writer Graham Hancock tells it his own way, crediting Crick's 1981 book Life Itself. He describes a seeded spaceship that "collided with the early Earth" some 3.9 billion years ago and "spilled out its contents of bacteria." It is told because, coming from Crick, the idea that someone deliberately planted life here carries a weight it would not otherwise have.
